written: 2026-10-01, before any stripe code was simulated and before any code was scored against the stripe target
status: PRE-REGISTRATION of the stripe training and its replay checks (Stage 1 of the stripes pipeline). Each later analysis (knockout, sensitivity, mode ownership, phases, relay, wall counterfactuals, steering, modules confirmation) gets its own file, committed before its script runs.
question: On the frozen tissue of model 1888 (11x11, Gpol-only ring clamp, field on), can a mirror-symmetric ring code a0 + sum a_n cos(n theta), held for 301 iterations and released, write the interior stripes (the 'French flag', PolyPatterning_Design.md pattern 6) as a pattern at some moment after release? How many orders does it take, does the stripe last longer than the face did, and do the face's findings about the field's feedback and the release transfer?
registeredBefore: the first stripe training restart, any replay of a code against the stripe target, and any rescoring of stored codes against it. ALREADY SEEN (so these inform the predictions below and are not tested again): every face result - training (orders 0-6, 523,280 codes), the switch rule, the relay, the wall halves, the causal story, the steering sweep and the modules confirmation - and the loss of the old full-lattice 'stripes' models (best 1.86 against the face's 2.084, a different target and a backprop-trained clamp). NOT SEEN: the score, pattern or overlap of any code on the interior stripes.

target.name: StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5
target.definition: the 9x9 interior (rows 1-9, columns 1-9) cut into three stripes of 3 columns x 9 rows: left flank (columns 1-3), centre stripe (columns 4-6) and right flank (columns 7-9), 27 cells each. The centre stripe is held at -60 mV; every other cell, the 54 flank cells and the 40 ring cells, at -5 mV. No ring cell is part of any stripe: the ring carries the code only and is scored at the background value, exactly as for the face (FaceMinus60Minus5).
target.symmetry: left-right and top-bottom symmetric. Every code a has a twin (a_n -> (-1)^n a_n) that gives the vertically flipped pattern, which is the same stripes, so 'the trained code' is one of a pair.

design.model: checkpoint 1888 unchanged; hold 301 iterations on the 40 ring cells, then released; 3000 iterations in all; ceiling 1.3 (every held value in [0, 1.3]), as for the face
design.score: balanced RMS against the target: the mean over two groups of each group's RMS error, features (the 27 centre-stripe cells) and other (the other 94 cells), at every iteration from the release (301) to 2999; a code's score is the lowest value, and its best moment the iteration where it occurs
design.stripeOverlap: structural intersection over union of the hyperpolarised interior cells (Vmem < -34.6 mV) with the 27 centre-stripe cells, boundaryCodeUtilities.structuralIntersectionOverUnion(vmem, centreStripeCellIndices); read at a code's best moment. The stripes are 'formed' when it is >= 0.9, the face's own criterion for the face's shape.
design.search: learnBoundaryHarmonics11x11.py (CMA-ES, unchanged): 150 generations at population 16 in the pilot, 100 at population 64 in the full run; even-numbered restarts start from the library, odd from a random allowed code (hit-and-run). The library is the stored dial and harmonic sweeps (target-independent) plus the codes the same folder's earlier arms have already simulated; no face-trained code is in it (no --libraryDirs).
design.pilot: data/boundaryHarmonicTraining1888Hold301StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5/: 20 restarts (0-19) of each of orders 0-0, 0-1, 0-2, 0-3 and of the even-only orders {0, 2} (--orders 0,2), arms run one after another in that order. Launcher: runLearnBoundaryHarmonics.sh with extraArguments='--target stripesInterior --targetName StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5'.
design.fullRun: only if the gate below is met: data/boundaryHarmonicTraining1888Hold301StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5Population64/: population 64, 10 restarts of each of orders 0-3, 0-4, 0-5, 0-6 and the even-only sets {0, 2, 4} and {0, 2, 4, 6}.
design.controls: 64 random allowed codes per contiguous code size (hit-and-run, scored as in training), the tissue with no clamp scored the same way (best moment in 301-2999), and the best of the stored sweep codes rerun and scored (the face summary's bestSweepCode analogue). Run by the existing analyzeBoundaryHarmonicTraining11x11.py, given the stripe target.
design.replays: the best code of the smallest contiguous size that meets the gate: (a) 20,000 iterations with the ring released at 301; (b) the same with fieldEnabled False; (c) the ring held for all 3000 iterations. Same replay helpers as the face.

V1.claim: the target is what is written above
V1.criterion: before any run: 27 cells at -60 mV (interior rows 1-9, columns 4-6), 54 flank cells and 40 ring cells at -5 mV, no ring cell in any stripe, the three stripes tiling the interior (checked; printed by the dry check)

V2.criterion: every held value of every code lies in [0, ceiling]

V3.criterion: the best code of each arm, replayed single-sample, reproduces its stored best score and best moment to within 1e-6 mV

V4.criterion: structuralIntersectionOverUnion without a target argument returns the face value it returned before the change (checked: 0.9333 on the orders 0-3 face code, equal to the stored value)

V5.criterion: every output is a new file under a name carrying StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5; the training script refuses an existing path

gate.claim: the stripes are reachable by this tissue and code
gate.criterion: G1: at least one restart of orders <= 6 ends with stripe overlap >= 0.9 at its best moment; AND G2: that code's score is at least 5 mV lower than the best of the 64 random allowed codes of its code size. If G1 and G2 hold, Stages 2-4 and the interactive relay movie go ahead. If G1 fails for every pilot arm at ceiling 1.3, the pilot is repeated once with ceiling 2.0 (same arms, same criteria, folder suffix Ceiling2, as the face's outline runs did) and the full run uses whichever ceiling met the gate, both reported. If it fails at 2.0 too, the report is the negative result with the pilot's scores, the controls and the limiting factors.

predictions.name: S1-stripesAreReachable
predictions.basis: the face was reached at order 3; the old stripes model trained to a lower loss than the face
predictions.criterion: at least one restart across the pilot and the full run has stripe overlap >= 0.9 at its best moment

predictions.name: S2-fewerOrdersThanTheFace
predictions.basis: the face needed order 3; the stripes depend on the column only, and an even order (the oval, order 2) already separates the ring's top and bottom from its sides
predictions.claim: the stripes need no more than the oval
predictions.criterion: the smallest contiguous code size with a restart at overlap >= 0.9 is <= 2 (the face's was 3)

predictions.name: S3-oddOrdersAddNothing
predictions.basis: the target is top-bottom symmetric, and odd orders break that symmetry
predictions.claim: dropping the odd orders costs nothing
predictions.criterion: the best score of orders {0, 2} is no more than 1.0 mV above that of orders 0-2 (20 restarts each, pilot); and, in the full run, the best of {0, 2, 4} is no more than 1.0 mV above that of 0-4

predictions.name: S4-bestCodesAreTopBottomSymmetric
predictions.basis: same symmetry; the face's best codes carry |a1| 0.21-0.26 and |a3| 0.15-0.32 because the face is not symmetric
predictions.claim: the best codes carry little odd-order content
predictions.criterion: for the best code of every contiguous size that reaches overlap >= 0.9, |a_n| <= 0.10 (G_pol / G_ref) for every odd n

predictions.name: S5-moreRestartsSucceed
predictions.basis: at order 3, 14 of the face's 30 restarts ended below 10 mV (47%)
predictions.claim: the stripes are found at least as reliably as the face
predictions.criterion: at order 3, population 16, at least 10 of the 20 pilot restarts end with overlap >= 0.9

predictions.name: S6-theStripePersists
predictions.basis: the face passed through its shape once, for 55-119 iterations in 20,000; the stripes are coarse and low in spatial frequency, so the field's sweep may hold them longer
predictions.claim: the stripes last longer than the face did
predictions.criterion: in the 20,000-iteration replay of the gate's best code, the longest run of consecutive iterations after the release with overlap >= 0.9 is >= 150 (the face's longest was 119)

predictions.name: S7-theFieldIsRequired
predictions.basis: face: with the field off, not one cell goes dark (27.4-27.5 mV)
predictions.claim: the stripes need the field's feedback too
predictions.criterion: with fieldEnabled False, no interior cell is below -34.6 mV at any iteration after the release

predictions.name: S8-theReleaseIsRequired
predictions.basis: face: held for all 3000 iterations only 21-57% of the face appeared
predictions.claim: the code does not draw the stripes while it is held
predictions.criterion: with the ring held for all 3000 iterations, overlap is < 0.9 at every iteration

controls.C1-randomCodesDoNotMakeStripes: none of the 64 random allowed codes of any contiguous size reaches overlap >= 0.9 at its best moment
controls.C2-noClampBaseline: descriptive: the tissue with no clamp, best moment in 301-2999, score and overlap
controls.C3-storedSweepBaseline: descriptive: the best stored sweep code rerun, score and overlap

reporting: Every criterion is reported verbatim with its number, including those that fail or reverse. The ceiling rule above is applied as written and both ceilings are shown if both are run. Anything computed beyond this file (ring cells at the ceiling, the coefficients, snapshots, face-code rescoring, the stripe's edges and uniformity, the no-buffer geometry at the stripe's ends) is labelled exploratory.
notRegisteredHere: knockouts with size-matched random controls, single-coefficient sensitivity, Fourier mode ownership and the field's roughness of the code-to-pattern map, the phases and the switch rule on the stripe code, the relay and its wall counterfactuals, the steering sweep and the modules; each is registered in its own file before it is run, with the face's finding as a transfer prediction.
